texts.li: {B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef}, as kindly as {B_pronoun} could manage, whether {A_pronoun} might sit downwind at supper. {A_nameDef} took {A_possessive} bowl outside and didn't come back.
{B_nameDef} opened every window in the room the moment {A_nameDef} walked in. {A_nameDef} noticed. Everyone noticed.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that a helixan can smell rot under a floor from across the room, and that {B_nameDef}'s bedroll needed burning. {B_nameDef} did not take it well.

{B_nameDef} sat down next to {A_nameDef} at supper, where nobody else ever sits, and talked to {A_objective} about the harvest as if it were the most ordinary thing in the world. It was, to {B_nameDef}.
{B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} about the day {A_pronoun} came here, and listened to the whole answer without once looking away.
{A_nameDef} flinched when {B_nameDef} reached for {A_possessive} hand. {B_nameDef} waited, and {A_nameDef} gave it.
{B_nameDef} couldn't meet {A_nameDef}'s eyes across the table, and said afterwards it felt like being read from the inside.
{A_nameDef} answered a question {B_nameDef} had only been thinking about. {B_nameDef} has been keeping to the far side of the colony since.
{B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef}, very politely, to stop doing whatever it was {A_pronoun} was doing. {A_nameDef} said {A_pronoun} wasn't doing anything. That was worse.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that the little carved figure by {B_possessive} bed was an obscenity and ought to be burned. {B_nameDef} moved it to a higher shelf and stopped speaking to {A_nameDef}.
{A_nameDef} turned the painting in the hall to face the wall. {B_nameDef} turned it back. This went on all afternoon.
{B_nameDef} wore {B_possessive} lucky charm to supper. {A_nameDef} looked at it the whole meal, and said one word about it afterwards, which was one too many.

{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that a bow is a coward's weapon, and that real glory is had close enough to smell the other fellow's breath. {B_nameDef} said {B_pronoun} would keep {B_possessive} distance, thanks, from both.
{A_nameDef} wouldn't eat at the same table as {B_nameDef} after the last fight, because {B_nameDef} had done all of {B_possessive} fighting from behind the wall.
{A_nameDef} walked the walls with {B_nameDef} after dark and showed {B_objective} every weak spot, and which ones {A_pronoun} meant to mend first.
{A_nameDef} taught {B_nameDef} where to stand in a doorway so a whole raid has to come at you one at a time. {B_nameDef} said it was the most comforting thing anyone had told {B_objective} all year.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} sat up late going over the colony's defences on a scrap of hide, and only stopped when the candle ran out.
